theme: using evidence to understand and describe friendship activities
can_do: Find audience, schedule, place and activities in a short youth programme notice.
Check a statement against an email and replace incorrect information with text evidence.
Compare a fictional learner profile with activity requirements and explain a decision.
Identify a fictional person from a short spoken description of appearance and personality.
Collect four categories of notes and shape them into a short diary paragraph.

language_focus.function: judge a claim against a text and replace only the incorrect detail
state whether an activity fits a profile and support the decision with evidence
keep visible features, personality and interests in distinct information groups
use a consistent person and pronoun across a short first-person paragraph

skill_targets.reading: Scan short functional texts, verify claims and combine details for a simple decision.
skill_targets.listening: Move from action recognition to person identification and one-word or one-number detail capture.
skill_targets.speaking: Ask for four information categories about a fictional friend and give a short reason.
skill_targets.writing: Organise notes into a coherent diary paragraph of roughly fifty words without exposing real personal data.

common_errors: answer a scan question from general knowledge instead of the visible text
mark a statement false without replacing the incorrect detail
choose suitability from one attractive trait while ignoring a key requirement
write more than one word in a one-word listening blank
switch the described person or pronoun inside one paragraph
give a preference without a supporting reason

skills_1.purpose: Locate a requested fact in newly written notices for age-appropriate clubs and programmes.
Judge a claim against a newly written message, then select the supporting correction.
Sort profile details into appearance, personality, interest and current-action evidence.
Compare a fictional profile with two or more programme requirements and choose an evidence-based decision.
Assemble a preference plus one logically connected reason.

skills_2.purpose: Listen to an original short sentence and select the matching action represented by accessible text and an icon.
Identify one fictional character from an original spoken description with contrasting features.
Capture exactly one word or one number from an original audio prompt.
Match a question about a fictional friend to an answer of the correct information type.
Order and complete sentences into a safe fictional diary paragraph with consistent reference.

pedagogy_constraints: Introduce scan targets before timed reading rounds.
Require visible or spoken evidence for every correctness and suitability decision.
Use original recorded or synthesised scripts for listening games; never infer missing textbook audio.
Keep one-word or one-number answer limits explicit and accessible.
Do not ask learners to disclose a real friend's identifying details.
Assess free writing with a transparent content-and-cohesion checklist, not exact-string matching.
originality_constraints: Do not reuse the source programme name, dates, location, contact details, email, characters, profiles, prompts or diary stems.
Do not reproduce, crop, trace or imitate the textbook advertisements, portraits, picture scenes or page layout.
Create all notices, messages, listening scripts, fictional profiles, distractors, feedback and visual assets from this clean brief only.
Use Vietnamese two-word names for newly designed characters.
Give every game concise source-aware help, deterministic answers, ten rounds and keyboard-accessible controls.
